UnitStatement: Crate rule_check_runner provides end-to-end rule-check orchestration for user-owned rule packs (completion plan C4 — end-to-end rule checks on authored models).

The runner wires three engine crates into one runnable path: the completeness checker (required inputs present), the rule_pack_document codec (decode the frozen-grammar formula AST), and the expression evaluator (compute the formula and the acceptability comparison).
Per check, the runner produces one of three automatic rule-check statuses — RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE, USER_RULE_CHECKED, USER_RULE_FAILED — and aggregates them worst-of.

The runner is pure in-memory orchestration: it does not parse text, execute host-language code, access files or network, spawn processes, load plugins, store private data, embed protected standards content, or emit professional/certification/sealing/authentication/approval/code-compliance claims.
Acceptability composition: a check whose formula evaluates to a boolean uses that boolean directly as the acceptability predicate.

A check whose formula evaluates to a quantity (e.g. a ratio) is compared against the single user-supplied limit named by the check's value_slot_refs, via a synthesized Compare(formula, relation, limit) evaluated through the same evaluator.

Before the evaluator boundary, B2/B3 unit normalization converts compatible DEC-018 catalog units to the declaration's unit; exact non-catalog demonstration units remain valid only when entered and declared unit strings match; incompatible or unknown unit substitutions block rather than evaluating.

The acceptability relation is the check's optional acceptability_relation member (TP-C4-ACCEPTREL-001), one of four ordering relations less_than/less_than_or_equal/greater_than/greater_than_or_equal, defaulting to less_than_or_equal when absent (backward compatible).

An explicit but unrecognized acceptability_relation token blocks the check rather than defaulting silently; the member is an additive PROPOSAL awaiting human ratification, and equality acceptance is a deliberate non-goal.
Input binding is a C4-defined minimal mechanism: the schema carries no selector tying a solver_result required input to a solved result row, so the binding is caller-supplied.
Solver values are supplied via SolverResultBinding (caller extracts {value, unit} for an input_id from a solved mechanics envelope); user values and limit slots via SuppliedValueBinding.

private_library_value inputs are resolved via LibraryValueBinding (C3 rule-pack/library reference wiring): the caller reads {value, unit} from the referenced private library record's value slot named by the rule pack's library_value_ref member in the local store.

A private_library_value input with no resolved library binding stays unsupplied (never a silent pass) with a recorded note; the library value is resolved at run time and never embedded in the rule pack (IP boundary).
DOCUMENT_KIND is the document-kind tag on a serialized run result: 'openpipestress.rule_check.run'.

PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY_NOTICE is carried on every run result: software rule-check evidence only; not a professional, certification, sealing, authentication, approval, or code-compliance claim; human review remains required.
Struct SolverResultBinding represents one solver value the caller resolved from a solved mechanics envelope for a solver_result required input (fields input_id, result_id, value, unit).

Struct SuppliedValueBinding represents one user-entered value for a user_supplied_rule_value required input or a value_slot limit; dimension is the snake_case dimension token (fields ref_id, value, unit, dimension).

Struct LibraryValueBinding represents one value the caller resolved from a saved private library for a private_library_value required input; the value is never embedded in the rule pack and stays in the private library (IP boundary).

Struct RuleCheckRunInput carries inputs to a rule-check run: rule_pack_document, solver_results, supplied_values, library_values, and current analysis statuses; the caller is expected to have already run document validation.

Enum RuleCheckStatus is the three automatic rule-check statuses the runner may emit (RuleInputsIncomplete, UserRuleChecked, UserRuleFailed); MODEL_INCOMPLETE, MECHANICS_SOLVED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, and HUMAN_APPROVED_FOR_PROJECT are intentionally not producible here.
RuleCheckStatus::as_str maps each status variant to its canonical screaming-snake-case string token.
RuleCheckStatus::severity_rank defines worst-of precedence: failed (2) > incomplete (1) > checked (0).
Struct ComputedQuantity is a computed or limit quantity surfaced in a check outcome (fields value, dimension, unit_ref).
Struct BoundInput records what a single rule-pack input resolved to for a check (input_id, source_kind, supplied flag, optional value/unit/result_id/note).
Struct RunFinding is a finding surfaced from completeness or evaluation, traced to its engine (fields code, severity, subject_id, message).

Struct CheckOutcome is the outcome of one check_definition, carrying check_id, status, optional computed_value and limit_value, the governing acceptability_relation, bound_inputs, completeness/evaluator findings, and diagnostic_codes.
Struct RuleCheckRunResult is the result of a run over all of a pack's checks (document_kind, rule_pack_id, grammar_version, aggregate_status, checks, professional_boundary_notice).
Function run_rule_checks runs every check_definition in the rule pack against the caller-resolved values and returns per-check outcomes plus a worst-of aggregate.
run_rule_checks collects per-check outcomes by mapping run_one_check over the document's check_definitions array.
When a pack has no checks, the aggregate status is RuleInputsIncomplete; otherwise it is the worst-of reduction over each check's status by severity_rank.

Struct RunContext holds the per-run indices (required_inputs, value_slots, formula_declarations) and the caller-supplied binding maps (solver_by_input, supplied_by_ref, library_by_input) plus current_statuses and grammar_version.
Struct ResolvedValue is a value resolved for a required input, ready to bind into the evaluator (value, unit, eval_dimension, binding_source).

Function run_one_check resolves a single check: its check_id, declared result_statuses, and diagnostic_policy, then resolves required inputs, runs completeness, decodes and evaluates the formula, and composes acceptability.

When a check references an input id absent from the required_index, run_one_check pushes a blocking INVALID_REFERENCE completeness finding ('check references an undeclared required input') and skips it.

Each required input's supplied value is resolved per source kind: SolverResult from solver_by_input, PrivateLibraryValue from library_by_input, UserSuppliedRuleValue from supplied_by_ref, and any other kind falls back to supplied_by_ref.
A resolved private_library_value records a provenance note naming the library kind/id, record, and slot, and states the value stays in the private library and is never embedded in the rule pack.
An unresolved private_library_value records a note that it has no resolved library reference (missing library_value_ref or the library/record/slot was not found) and is treated as unsupplied.
Each supplied value is normalized to the declared unit via normalize_value_to_declared_unit; a normalization error pushes an evaluator finding and leaves the value/unit unset.
A supplied value with a known dimension passes the completeness gates via the private-reviewed constructor; otherwise the input is left unsupplied so completeness blocks (never a silent pass).
run_one_check runs check_completeness over the assembled required and supplied inputs plus the current statuses, mapping each completeness finding into a RunFinding.

If completeness readiness is Blocked or any blocking completeness finding exists, the check returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with a missing_input diagnostic and acceptability_relation 'none', without evaluating the formula.
The formula is resolved from the formula_index by the check's formula_ref ref_id; an undeclared formula pushes a blocking INVALID_REFERENCE finding and blocks after completeness.
A formula declaration with no declaration_payload.expression_ast pushes a blocking INVALID_REFERENCE finding and blocks after completeness.
The expression AST is decoded via decode_expression; a decode error pushes a blocking DECODE_ERROR finding and blocks after completeness.

The formula's variable references are bound to resolved values; a resolved value with a known eval_dimension binds a Quantity, otherwise it binds a missing VariableBinding (never a silent substitution).

The formula is computed by evaluate over the EvaluationInput (expression, bindings, required_variable_ids, current statuses, declared grammar version); any evaluator finding blocks after completeness.
When the formula evaluates to a Boolean, true yields USER_RULE_CHECKED and false yields USER_RULE_FAILED, with acceptability_relation 'formula_predicate'.

When the formula evaluates to a Quantity, the top-level acceptability relation is resolved (computed relation limit); an unsupported acceptability_relation token pushes a blocking RULE_EVALUATOR_ERROR and returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with relation 'none'.

For a quantity check, the limit is resolved via resolve_limit; a resolution error or absent limit returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE (with RULE_INPUT_MISSING when no user-supplied value-slot limit is available).
The limit quantity is built from the limit value, unit, and dimension; missing or unknown unit/dimension metadata pushes a blocking RULE_EVALUATOR_ERROR and returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE.

The acceptability comparison evaluates Expression::Compare(operator, formula_quantity, limit_quantity) through the same evaluator; Boolean true yields USER_RULE_CHECKED, false yields USER_RULE_FAILED, otherwise RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE.

Function resolve_limit resolves a check's governing limit from the first value_slot_refs entry, taking the numeric value from the caller's supplied-value map keyed by slot id, and returns (value, unit, eval_dimension).
resolve_limit prefers the value_slot's declared dimension and unit_ref from the value_slot_index, falling back to the binding's dimension/unit, then normalizes the value to the declared unit.

Function normalize_value_to_declared_unit returns the value unchanged when entered and declared unit strings match; missing declared/entered unit metadata or a 'TBD' declared unit yields a blocking UnitMismatch finding.

normalize_value_to_declared_unit resolves the dimension and the entered/declared unit symbols and converts via convert_for_dimension; an unknown dimension, incompatible unit, or failed conversion yields a blocking UnitMismatch finding.
Function unit_mismatch_finding builds a blocking UnitMismatch RunFinding describing that an entered unit cannot be normalized to the declared unit for the given dimension, with a reason.
Function resolve_acceptability_relation resolves a check's acceptability relation (computed relation limit) to a frozen-grammar comparison operator.
An absent acceptability_relation member resolves to LessThanOrEqual, preserving historical behaviour for packs authored before the additive member existed (the sole documented default).
An explicit but unrecognized acceptability_relation token is never silently defaulted; resolve_acceptability_relation returns Err(token) so the caller blocks the check (no-silent-defaults, CONTRACT).
resolve_acceptability_relation maps tokens less_than, less_than_or_equal, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal to their operators; empty string maps to LessThanOrEqual; any other token returns Err.
Function acceptability_relation_label gives the canonical string label for an acceptability relation operator, reported on the check outcome so the GUI shows the governing relation.
Function quantity_to_computed converts an evaluator Quantity into a ComputedQuantity, encoding the dimension to its document token and copying value and unit_ref.
Function blocked_after_completeness returns a RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE CheckOutcome with an evaluator_error diagnostic and acceptability_relation 'none' for checks that block after completeness passed.

Function enforce_declared keeps an emitted status inside the check's declared result_statuses envelope; an undeclared status is downgraded to RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with a blocking STATUS_NOT_DECLARED finding.
Function push_diagnostic appends a diagnostic code resolved from the check's diagnostic_policy for a given key, de-duplicating already-present codes.
Function index_by builds a HashMap from an array member of the document keyed by each item's id field.

Function source_kind_from_token maps source-kind tokens (solver_result, model_input, user_supplied_rule_value, private_library_value, owner_design_basis) to SourceKind, defaulting unknown tokens to Tbd.
Function required_for_from_token maps required-for tokens (rule_check, reporting, diagnostic) to RequiredFor, defaulting unknown tokens to Tbd.
Function severity_str maps a FindingSeverity (Info, Warning, Blocking) to its lowercase string.
Function to_automatic_status maps an evaluator AnalysisStatus to a completeness AutomaticAnalysisStatus; HumanApprovedForProject maps to HumanReviewRequired.

Function completeness_dimension_from_token maps a snake_case dimension token to the completeness checker's dimension by routing through the document codec's evaluator-dimension decode (single source of truth for the token vocabulary).
Function eval_dimension_to_completeness maps each evaluator Dimension variant to the corresponding completeness Dimension variant.
rule_check_runner unit tests use a minimal invented rule pack (one ratio check actual/limit against a ratio limit value slot); all values are invented non-engineering content.
Test passing_check_yields_user_rule_checked: ratio 0.5 with default relation yields USER_RULE_CHECKED with a dimensionless ratio computed value and no findings.
Test failing_check_yields_user_rule_failed: ratio 1.5 yields USER_RULE_FAILED.
Test missing_solver_input_blocks_without_evaluating: a missing solver binding yields RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with no computed value, relation 'none', and a RULE_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic.
Test missing_limit_slot_blocks_as_incomplete: the ratio computes (0.5) but with no limit slot the check is RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE and limit_value is none.
Test unit_mismatch_between_ratio_and_limit_blocks: a limit slot declared with a non-ratio unit/dimension yields RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with a RULE_EVALUATOR_ERROR diagnostic.
Test compatible_rule_check_units_normalize_to_declared_units: MPa and kPa inputs normalize to the declared Pa unit before evaluation, yielding USER_RULE_CHECKED with normalized bound-input values.

Test incompatible_rule_check_units_block_before_evaluation: a length unit (mm) against a declared Pa stress unit yields RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with a UnitMismatch finding and the input left unsupplied, no formula evaluation.
Test status_outside_declared_result_statuses_is_downgraded: a computed PASS not in the declared result_statuses is downgraded to RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with a STATUS_NOT_DECLARED finding.
Test aggregate_is_worst_of_across_checks: a pass on one check and a fail on a stricter check yields an aggregate of USER_RULE_FAILED.
Test private_library_value_is_unsupplied_not_silently_passed: a private_library_value input with no library binding is unsupplied with a note, yielding RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE.

Test private_library_value_resolves_from_library_binding_and_passes: a private-library limit resolved via LibraryValueBinding yields USER_RULE_CHECKED with a provenance note containing 'private library', the library id, and 'never embedded'.
Test private_library_value_with_failing_library_value_reports_failure: ratio 50/40 = 1.25 > 1.0 yields USER_RULE_FAILED.
Test emits_only_the_automatic_status_vocabulary: the serialized result must not contain HUMAN_APPROVED_FOR_PROJECT, Certified, Sealed, Approved, or code_compliant, and must contain USER_RULE_CHECKED.

Integration test acceptability_relation_run exercises the additive optional acceptability_relation member on a CheckDefinition (TP-C4-ACCEPTREL-001) over the invented example rule pack; the member is backward compatible (absent uses less_than_or_equal).
Test greater_than_or_equal_relation_flips_the_acceptance: under >=, ratio 0.5 fails and ratio 1.5 passes — inverting the default <= cases.
Test less_than_relation_is_strict_at_the_boundary: ratio exactly 1.0 passes under <= but fails under strict <, witnessing the relation drives the result.
Test explicit_less_than_or_equal_matches_the_absent_default: the explicit less_than_or_equal token reproduces the historical hard-coded behaviour (ratio 1.0 <= 1.0 passes).
Test unrecognized_relation_blocks_rather_than_defaulting: an explicit unsupported token (e.g. 'between') blocks at RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with relation 'none' and a RULE_EVALUATOR_ERROR finding.

Integration test invented_demo_run is an end-to-end rule-check run over the repository's invented example rule pack (examples/rule_packs/invented_demo.yaml, DEL-06-05) using the frozen-grammar evaluator and <= acceptability.

Test example_pack_passing_run_is_user_rule_checked: solver 50 and limit 100 yield rule_pack_id invented_demo_rule_pack, grammar_version 1.0.0, USER_RULE_CHECKED, and a dimensionless ratio computed value of 0.5.
Test example_pack_failing_run_is_user_rule_failed: solver 150 yields USER_RULE_FAILED with a computed ratio of 1.5.
Test example_pack_missing_solver_input_is_rule_inputs_incomplete: dropping the solver binding yields RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with no computed value and relation 'none'.

Crate open_pipe_stress_rule_pack_document is the rule-pack document seam: production codec between the rule-pack JSON document encoding and the frozen DEC-022 expression AST, JCS checksum computation, and document-level lifecycle validation; no text parsing, no protected content, no compliance claims.
rule_pack_document depends on the expression_evaluator, rule_pack_lifecycle, and canonical_json crates plus serde and serde_json.

Crate rule_pack_document (Phase C2 backend, DEC-022 basis) is the production bridge between rule-pack JSON documents (schemas/rule_pack.schema.yaml) and the frozen expression grammar in the expression evaluator.
The codec maps between the node-tagged JSON expression encoding (pinned by fixtures/rule_expressions/conformance_corpus/) and the evaluator's typed AST.
The crate computes the RFC 8785 (JCS) checksum over a pack document with the checksums member excluded, grammar-version-bound per DEC-022 through the rule_pack_lifecycle crate.
The crate provides document-level validation surfacing lifecycle, grammar, expression, and checksum findings for the desktop editor.

The crate does not parse expression text (a writable text syntax awaits the D-02b human ruling), does not store private payloads, does not choose storage paths, and emits no professional/certification/sealing/authentication/code-compliance claims.

CHECKSUM_PAYLOAD_EXCLUDES is the document member excluded from the canonical checksum payload ('checksums'); the checksum cannot cover itself, and the exclusion is recorded in checksum evidence as payload_excludes.
CHECKSUM_BASIS is the stable label for how rule-pack document checksums are computed: 'rfc8785_jcs_sha256_excluding_checksums'.

DIMENSION_TOKENS is the canonical mapping between snake_case document dimension tokens and the evaluator Dimension enum (dimensionless, length, mass, time, temperature, stress, pressure, moment, etc., plus TBD).
Function decode_dimension decodes a snake_case dimension token from the document vocabulary into a Dimension, or None when unknown.
Function encode_dimension encodes an evaluator Dimension as its document token (every Dimension variant has a token).
Struct DecodeError is a decode failure with a JSON-path-style breadcrumb (path, message) for editor diagnostics.
Helper object() requires a JSON value to be an object, returning a DecodeError otherwise.
Helper member() fetches a required map member, returning a DecodeError 'missing required member' otherwise.
Helper string_member()/number_member() fetch a required member as a string or finite number, returning a DecodeError on type mismatch.
Helper optional_bool() reads an optional boolean member with a default.
Function decode_quantity decodes a quantity object (value, dimension, unit_ref, optional unit_required and dimension_check_required defaulting true); an unknown dimension token is a DecodeError.

Function decode_table decodes a UserTable (table_id, argument/result dimensions and unit_refs, and rows of argument/result numbers); unknown dimension tokens or a non-array rows member are DecodeErrors.
Function decode_expression decodes a node-tagged JSON expression into the evaluator AST.

decode_expression accepts the full corpus encoding including the evaluator refusal markers unsupported_form / unsafe_host_access, which always evaluate to blocking findings; pack-document validation and the schema additionally reject refusal markers as authorable content.

decode_expression dispatches on the node tag: literal, variable_ref, unary, binary, compare, logical, select, aggregate, interpolate, lookup, unsupported_form, unsafe_host_access; an unknown node kind is a DecodeError.
Unary nodes accept operators negate, abs, not; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Binary nodes accept operators add, subtract, multiply, divide; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Compare nodes accept operators less_than, less_than_or_equal, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal, equal, not_equal; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Logical nodes accept operators and, or; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Select nodes decode a condition and then/else branches.
Aggregate nodes accept functions min, max over an operands array; an unknown function or non-array operands is a DecodeError.
Interpolate nodes decode a table plus an argument expression.
Lookup nodes accept modes exact, step over a table and an argument; an unknown mode is a DecodeError.
Function encode_expression encodes an evaluator AST back into the node-tagged JSON encoding, the inverse of decode_expression across every node kind.

Function expression_contains_refusal_marker returns true when an expression tree contains an evaluator refusal marker (UnsupportedForm or UnsafeHostAccess); refusal markers are engine vocabulary, never authorable pack content.
Struct DocumentError is a document-level failure (subject, message) that prevents checksum computation or validation.
Function canonical_payload_bytes returns the RFC 8785 canonical byte payload a rule-pack checksum covers: the document with the CHECKSUM_PAYLOAD_EXCLUDES members removed.
Struct ComputedRulePackChecksum is serializable checksum evidence (algorithm, canonicalization, payload_scope, payload_ref, payload_excludes, basis, grammar_version, grammar_version_bound, value).

Function compute_rule_pack_checksum computes the grammar-version-bound JCS checksum of a rule-pack document; the canonicalization label is 'JCS' because the function produces canonical bytes itself via canonical_json (RFC 8785).
compute_rule_pack_checksum requires a rule_pack_id and a top-level grammar_version (DEC-022), returning a DocumentError when either is missing.
Struct ValidationFinding is a document validation finding (code, subject, message, blocking).
Struct FormulaValidation reports per-formula validation (formula_id, declaration_form, decode_status, findings).
Struct ChecksumValidation reports the declared value, recomputed checksum, and a match_status of match | mismatch_review_required | declared_placeholder | not_computable.

Struct RulePackDocumentValidation is the document validation envelope for the desktop editor; statuses describe software findings only and are not professional/certification/sealing/authentication/code-compliance claims.
Function map_privacy_class maps privacy_class tokens (public_schema_only, public_invented_example, private_user_data, private_project_data, quarantined) to PrivacyClass, defaulting to Tbd.

Function map_redistribution_status maps redistribution tokens (public_permissive, private_only, unknown, protected_suspected, invented_non_engineering_example) to RedistributionStatus, defaulting to Tbd.
Function map_review_status maps review_status tokens (pending, accepted, rejected, quarantined) to ReviewStatus, defaulting to Tbd.

The schema's lifecycle_status vocabulary is wider than the crate enum; since validate_lifecycle does not branch on the field, map_lifecycle_status maps unrepresentable tokens to Tbd rather than interpreting them.

Function lifecycle_finding_code maps each lifecycle finding code enum variant to its screaming-snake-case string (e.g. MISSING_GRAMMAR_VERSION, STALE_CHECKSUM, PROTECTED_CONTENT_SUSPECTED, PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION).
Function is_placeholder_checksum treats an empty or TBD-prefixed (case-insensitive) checksum value as a placeholder.

Function validate_rule_pack_document validates a rule-pack document: shape-critical members, grammar version, every declarative-AST formula payload, lifecycle/privacy/provenance findings, and the recorded checksum against a fresh JCS computation.
Validation requires rule_pack_kind to equal 'open_pipe_stress_rule_pack', pushing a blocking UNEXPECTED_DOCUMENT_KIND finding otherwise.

Validation requires a non-empty, strict-semver, evaluator-supported grammar_version; absence pushes blocking MISSING_GRAMMAR_VERSION and an unsupported version pushes blocking UNSUPPORTED_GRAMMAR_VERSION (evaluation would block, never best-effort).

Validation decodes each declarative_ast formula's expression_ast: a decoded refusal marker pushes blocking REFUSAL_MARKER_AUTHORED, a decode failure pushes blocking EXPRESSION_DECODE_FAILED, and a missing AST pushes blocking MISSING_EXPRESSION_AST.
Absence of formula_declarations pushes a blocking MISSING_FORMULA_DECLARATIONS finding.

Validation recomputes the checksum and compares with the declared value, yielding declared_placeholder, match, mismatch_review_required, or not_computable; a mismatch pushes a blocking CHECKSUM_MISMATCH finding.
Validation runs lifecycle validation through the DEL-06-04 crate over a RulePackLifecycleRecord assembled from the document's classification, provenance, professional_boundary, and checksum metadata.
protected_content_suspected is true when provenance.protected_content_review is 'quarantined_protected_suspected' or the redistribution_status is ProtectedSuspected.
The ProfessionalBoundary record defaults the compliance/certification/sealing/software-generated-acceptance claim flags to true and human_review_required to false when absent (conservative defaults).

has_blocking_findings is true when any document, lifecycle, or per-formula finding is blocking; the validation envelope reports publicly_exportable and a professional-boundary notice stating no compliance claim is made and human review remains required.
rule_pack_document unit tests cover the codec round trip, decode breadcrumbs, refusal markers, checksum requirements, and validation; values are invented.
Test decodes_and_encodes_every_node_kind_round_trip: a nested AST covering select/logical/compare/unary/aggregate/binary/interpolate decodes, encodes, and decodes again unchanged.
Test decode_reports_breadcrumb_paths: a bad dimension token yields a DecodeError whose path is 'expression.right.quantity' and message contains the bad token.
Test refusal_markers_decode_but_are_flagged: an unsafe_host_access node decodes but expression_contains_refusal_marker reports it.
Test checksum_requires_grammar_version: a document lacking grammar_version fails checksum computation with subject 'grammar_version'.

Test checksum_excludes_checksums_member_and_binds_grammar_version: adding a checksums member does not change the checksum, payload_excludes is ['checksums'], and changing grammar_version changes the checksum.
Test validation_blocks_missing_grammar_version: a document without grammar_version yields blocking findings including MISSING_GRAMMAR_VERSION.

Integration test corpus_parity asserts codec parity against the blessed conformance corpus (TP-C1-GRAMMAR-001): every corpus expression decodes through the production codec and survives an encode->decode round trip unchanged.
Test every_corpus_expression_round_trips_through_the_production_codec: every case_*.json corpus expression decodes and round-trips unchanged, with an enforced floor of at least 60 cases.

Integration test invented_demo_document runs end-to-end checks over the invented example rule pack (DEL-06-05): the codec decodes its frozen-grammar AST, the evaluator computes the demonstration ratio, the stamped JCS checksum matches a fresh computation, and validation reports no blocking findings.
Test example_pack_expression_evaluates_the_invented_ratio: decoding and evaluating the example formula with solver 50 and limit 100 yields a dimensionless ratio quantity of 0.5 with no findings.
Test example_pack_stamped_checksum_matches_recomputation: the stamped checksum equals a fresh compute_rule_pack_checksum, is grammar-version-bound, and grammar_version is 1.0.0.

Test example_pack_document_validation_has_no_blocking_findings: validating the example pack yields no blocking findings, not lifecycle-blocked, supported grammar, publicly exportable, checksum match, and one decoded formula.

Crate open_pipe_stress_rule_pack_lifecycle (version 0.1.0, edition 2021, publish=false) handles private rule-pack lifecycle and checksum handling for OpenPipeStress, with lib path src/lib.rs and no dependencies.

The rule_pack_lifecycle crate is the bounded implementation slice for DEL-06-04: it records rule-pack lifecycle metadata, privacy/redistribution state, checksum evidence, and audit/report-facing manifest hooks without storing private rule-pack payloads in the public repository.

Scope: rule-pack identity, display name, schema version, rule-pack version, expression grammar version (DEC-022), lifecycle status, source notice, privacy class, redistribution status, review status, and protected-content review flags.

Scope: SHA-256 checksum records over caller-supplied payload bytes, with explicit metadata distinguishing caller-supplied JCS-compatible bytes from JSON canonicalization the crate has actually verified.
Scope: grammar-version checksum binding per DEC-022 — the declared strict-semver grammar_version must sit inside the JCS-hashed rule-pack payload bytes so the FR-016 reported checksum binds it.

The crate provides the exact JCS member encoding (grammar_version_jcs_member), a byte-containment evidence check (payload_declares_grammar_version, a necessary-condition check on caller bytes, not JSON parsing), and a binding-enforcing checksum constructor.

Scope: deterministic lifecycle findings for missing source notices, missing/unknown redistribution state, missing/malformed/unbound grammar versions, missing/stale checksums, suspected protected content, attempted public export of private content, and professional-boundary violations.
Scope: audit-manifest references that expose only identity, version, grammar version, checksum, source notice, and privacy/redistribution metadata.

Boundary: the crate does not parse or canonicalize JSON, implement storage paths, encrypt private rule packs, manage access control, handle secrets, run a GUI, render reports, define API transport, or evaluate engineering/code rules; callers own canonical JSON serialization before hashing.
Boundary: the grammar-version binding check is byte containment over caller-supplied bytes, never JSON parsing; PKG-12 owns storage, access, and secret-handling policy.

Verification: unit tests cover deterministic SHA-256 checksums, unverified caller-supplied JCS-byte metadata, missing-metadata diagnostics, grammar-version findings, the binding-enforcing constructor, private export blocking, protected-content quarantine, stale checksum detection, audit hook redaction, and professional-boundary enforcement.

Verification: the golden checksum-binding corpus fixtures/rule_expressions/checksum_binding/ pins byte/hash stability and the DEC-022 property that changing or removing the grammar_version member changes the rule-pack checksum.
